More than 15,000 suicides reported each year
item.description:
Suicide has emerged as a major public health problem in Bangladesh. According to police records, 76,361 people died by suicide between 2020 and 2024—an average of more than 15,000 a year. That is more than three times the World Health Organization (WHO)’s estimated figure for Bangladesh in 2021.

Young people are at relatively higher risk of suicide. Family and relationship conflicts, psychological distress, depression, unemployment, academic pressure and examinations, among other social, economic and mental health factors, can increase the risk. Experts say reliable data collection, accessible mental health services and restrictions on access to lethal means such as pesticides are essential for suicide prevention.

These issues were discussed at a suicide prevention meeting held at the International Centre for Diarrhoeal Disease Research, Bangladesh (icddr,b) in Dhaka on Sunday.

The meeting was organised jointly by the National Institute of Mental Health and Hospital, the World Health Organization and icddr,b under the WHO’s suicide prevention project, “Live Life: Suicide Prevention in Bangladesh.” Mental health and psychiatric specialists, researchers, police officials and representatives of various ministries attended the event.

Participants also recommended repealing or reforming the law that criminalises attempted suicide. Several speakers said people who attempt suicide are usually in deep distress and need treatment, support and compassion rather than punishment.

A deeply rooted problem

In the first presentation, Mohammad Sohel Shamik, deputy project coordinator of icddr,b’s Maternal and Child Health Division, highlighted the scale of the problem. He said the number of suicides recorded by Bangladesh Police was much higher than the WHO’s estimated figure. According to the WHO’s latest estimate, for 2021, around 4,714 people die by suicide in Bangladesh each year. Police records, however, indicate 14,000 to 15,000 suicides annually.

Participants were given a draft of the National Suicide Prevention Strategy 2026–2030. It contains suicide statistics for 2020–2024 and January–October 2025. The number of suicides was lowest in 2024, at 13,975, and highest in 2022, at 16,886. In 2021, there were 15,774 suicides—more than three times the WHO estimate. These deaths are generally recorded by police stations as unnatural deaths, with cases filed accordingly.

According to police data, the highest number of suicides occurred in Jashore. Between 2022 and 2025, 1,454 cases involving suicide were filed there. The other nine districts with relatively high numbers were Dhaka, Cumilla, Dinajpur, Bogura, Mymensingh, Kushtia, Pabna, Jhenaidah and Naogaon.

Mohammad Sohel Shomik and several other participants said not all suicides or suicide attempts are reported or recorded. There are also instances in which killings are reported as suicides.

Under Section 309 of the Penal Code, attempting suicide is a punishable offence, carrying a maximum sentence of one year’s simple imprisonment, a fine, or both. In cases of suicide resulting in death, police conduct an unnatural-death inquiry under Section 174 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. If someone is found to have abetted or assisted a suicide, Section 306 of the Penal Code provides for up to 10 years’ imprisonment and a fine.

In the second presentation, Anika Tasnim Hossain, an associate scientist at icddr,b’s Maternal and Child Health Division, said fear and stigma were among the reasons suicide and suicide attempts were underreported.

She said data on suicides and suicide attempts could be collected from three sources: hospitals and clinics, police stations and communities. Community members often have the best knowledge of such incidents, she said. Teachers, imams, village police officers, medicine-shop owners and agricultural extension officers could be important sources of information.

Combining information from these three sources would provide a more accurate picture, she said.

Anika Tasnim Hossain said a pilot project on the issue was being implemented in four upazilas under the WHO project: Shibganj in Chapainawabganj, Gowainghat in Sylhet, Abhaynagar in Jashore and Shailkupa in Jhenaidah.

Compassion instead of punishment

Professor Fowara Tasnim, additional director general (development and research) of the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) and chief guest at the event, said there needed to be serious consideration of whether attempted suicide could be removed from the list of criminal offences. If that was not possible, she said, the law should be reformed.

There is no provision for legal action against a person who dies by suicide. However, participants said the law provides for punishment of people who survive a suicide attempt. The provision was introduced during British rule. Although Britain has since repealed the law, it remains in Bangladesh and most countries around the world no longer criminalise attempted suicide.

Several psychiatrists and mental health specialists at the event said mental health problems increase the risk of suicide and suicide attempts. Mental health problems should not be treated as criminal behaviour, they said. People who survive suicide attempts should receive medical care and compassion rather than punishment.

Two physicians from the National Institute of Mental Health and Hospital argued for retaining some form of punishment, saying authorities should also consider cases in which threats of suicide are used to blackmail or pressure others.

Additional Deputy Inspector General of Police (Crime Metro) Md Ashraful Islam said the existence of the law deterred some people from attempting suicide. He claimed that one reason suicide rates were lower among government employees was that they knew an attempt could lead to a year in prison and seriously damage their careers.

Participants cited a study conducted across 171 countries which found that criminalising suicide attempts was associated with higher suicide rates. They also said suicide rates had fallen in Sri Lanka and Singapore after attempts were decriminalised.

Restricting access to pesticides

Pesticides, insecticides and herbicides are among the major means of suicide in Bangladesh. Most are used in agriculture, but there is little regulation or monitoring of their use.

They are readily available, and people often leave them unsecured after using them in fields, creating a risk for those experiencing psychological distress.

Participants said suicide rates had been reduced in Sri Lanka and South Korea after certain pesticides and herbicides were banned. Mohammad Sohel Shomik of icddr,b said that in some parts of India, farmers did not have direct access to pesticides.

Instead, pesticides were obtained and used collectively through cooperatives, with village councils overseeing and monitoring their use. This had helped reduce suicides among farmers, he said.

The event opened with remarks by Md Anisur Rahman, senior director of icddr,b’s Maternal and Child Health Division. WHO National Professional Officer Hasina Momtaz then said young people appeared to face a higher risk of suicide and that their vulnerabilities needed to be better understood. She also stressed the importance of responsible reporting by the media.

In her closing remarks, Professor Safiun Nahar, director of the National Institute of Mental Health and chair of the event, said policy reform was necessary and difficult, but pesticide regulation was achievable. Authorities needed to ensure that pesticides did not become easily accessible to everyone, she said.

item.title: IUB Beatrice Tinsley research scholarship for Women Researchers, information needed to know
item.description:
To increase women’s participation in science and research and facilitate access to higher education, the Centre for Astronomy, Space Science and Astrophysics (CASSA) at Independent University, Bangladesh (IUB) has launched the “Beatrice Tinsley Postbac Research Assistantship”.

It offers a unique opportunity for emerging women researchers with an interest in science.

Under an IUB-funded sponsored research grant, the fellowship will appoint two full-time research assistants.

The one-year paid fellowship programme is primarily designed for women who have already completed their bachelor’s degree and intend to pursue a higher graduate degree, such as a master’s or PhD, in the future.

Jannatul’s higher education dream comes true, receives Tk 7.4m scholarship

Selected researchers will have the opportunity to work full-time under the one-year fellowship during 2026–27. During this period, each Tinsley Research Associate will receive a monthly stipend of Tk 30,000.

Throughout the year-long programme, fellows will take part in original research, with the principal objective of publishing a full research paper as the first author based on their own research.

From Haor to Sheffield, story of Shamsul Alam of receiving 3 scholarships

The assistantship will also directly support fellows in developing strong application profiles to pursue higher education at internationally recognised graduate schools.

Candidates with strong academic merit and a keen interest in research can apply online. Full details of the application process and the official form are available at cassa.bd/tra.

For queries regarding the application process or the fellowship, applicants are advised to contact the programme directly by email at kasad@iub.edu.bd.

The fellowship programme is expected to serve as a milestone in the future careers of young women aspiring to pursue higher education and build careers in science and research.

item.title: Verdict on death references, appeals in Nusrat murder case today
item.description:
The High Court will deliver its verdict today, Monday, on the death references and appeals filed by the convicts in the Nusrat Jahan murder case. A High Court bench comprising Justice Bhishmadev Chakraborty and Justice KM Rasheduzzaman Raja will pronounce the verdict.

Police have tightened security at Nusrat Jahan’s family home in Sonagazi, Feni, ahead of the verdict.

Sonagazi Model Police Station officer-in-charge Abul Hasim said security was increased following a request from Nusrat’s brother and case complainant, Mahmudul Hasan. Two police officers had been deployed at the house since the murder.

Seven more officers were deployed there from Sunday, he said. Surveillance has also been increased in the area to maintain law and order.

The High Court concluded hearings on the death references, appeals and jail appeals in the case on 20 August and set Monday for the verdict.

Nusrat’s elder brother Mahmudul Hasan said, “My parents and the rest of my family want justice. We hope the lower court’s verdict will be upheld by the High Court as well.” He said the family was satisfied with the additional security but was “not completely free of concern” because family members have to leave the house for various reasons.

Nusrat murder: Charges against ex-Sonagazi OC found true

The Chief Justice formed the special bench on 10 June to hear death references, appeals and other matters under laws relating to violence against women and children on a priority basis.

The bench began proceedings on 14 June. Hearings in the Nusrat murder case began on 28 July and continued for 17 working days.

The case

According to court records, on 27 March 2019, Siraj Ud Daula, then principal of Sonagazi Islamia Fazil (Degree) Madrasah, summoned Nusrat to his office and sexually harassed her. He was arrested after a case was filed.

On 6 April, after Nusrat refused to withdraw the case, she was taken to the madrasah rooftop, where her hands and feet were tied, kerosene was poured over her and she was set on fire. She died on 10 April while undergoing treatment at the burn unit of Dhaka Medical College Hospital.

Her elder brother Mahmudul Hasan filed a case over the arson at Sonagazi police station. It was later converted into a murder case.

In its verdict on 24 October 2019, the Feni Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunal sentenced all 16 accused to death, including the suspended madrasah principal Siraj Ud Daula.

Sonagazi AL chief arrested over Nusrat murder

The other death-row convicts are Ruhul Amin, then president of Sonagazi upazila Awami League; Sonagazi municipality councillor Maksudul Alam; madrasah teacher Hafez Abdul Kader; lecturer Afsar Uddin; madrasah students Nur Uddin, Shahadat Hossain Shamim, Saifur Rahman Mohammad Zubayer, Javed Hossain alias Sakhawat Hossain Javed, Kamrun Nahar Moni, Umme Sultana Popy alias Tuhin, Abdur Rahim Sharif, Iftekhar Uddin Rana, Imran Hossain Mamun, Mohammad Shamim and Mahi Uddin Shakil.

After the trial court verdict, the case records were sent to the relevant High Court section on 29 October 2019 for a death reference and registered as Death Reference No. 140/2019.

A paper book was prepared on a priority basis because the case was considered sensational. The convicts also filed separate appeals and jail appeals.

item.title: Sundarbans climate project to close early amid UK aid cuts
item.description:
A UK-funded climate resilience project in Bangladesh is being forced to close two years ahead of schedule following cuts to Britain’s foreign aid budget, leaving thousands of vulnerable people without planned support and threatening to undermine work already carried out, according to The Independent.
The UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) is implementing cuts to the foreign aid budget that will reduce the UK aid budget from 0.5% to 0.3% of Gross National Income.
The cuts have affected aid programs in a number of developing countries, with observers describing them as a “moral catastrophe” and expressing particular concern over reductions in funding for climate projects, said the report.
Among those affected is British development charity Practical Action, which has managed part of a major development project in Bangladesh since 2023.
The project aims to improve the lives of tens of thousands of people through interventions including solar power systems, climate-resilient agriculture and aquaculture feedstocks and technologies, as well as weather information systems providing early warnings for extreme rainfall and cyclones.
The project is located in Bangladesh’s Sundarbans, the world’s largest tidal mangrove forest, much of which is a Unesco World Heritage Site. It began in 2023 and was originally expected to continue until 2028.
However, in April 2026, Practical Action was told that it would have to end its project in June this year, according to Tamanna Rahma, climate resilience lead for Practical Action Bangladesh. Following lobbying by the charity, the deadline was later extended to September, she said.
Practical Action was expected to receive £2.2 million by 2026, but received “far less than this”, Rahma said.
The project was originally expected to reach 57,000 people by the end of this year, but will ultimately reach around 37,000 people, according to Rahma.
“This abrupt cut has threatened our reputation in the community, which we have carefully built up over the past two and a half years,” Rahma said. “It has also impacted the long-term stability of the interventions that we have made, and limited our ability to plan for an effective exit.”
The reduction in funding for Practical Action’s project forms part of wider cuts to the UK-Bangladesh bilateral aid program, which is set to fall from £66.7 million to £31 million between 2025/26 and 2026/27, according to figures revealed in July and cited by The Independent.
Rahma said the early exit was particularly damaging because communities in the project area require continued support to adapt to the impacts of climate change.
“Every year we are seeing more severe storms and cyclones, while the sea is rising and soil is becoming salinated,” she said. “There is huge demand for financing such as this, yet the ability to make these kinds of tangible programmatic interventions is declining.”
The Sundarbans is situated on the Ganges Delta, where the Ganges, Brahmaputra and Meghna rivers converge before flowing into the Bay of Bengal.
The vast mangrove forest covers 10,277 square kilometres and is home to 42 mammal species, including endangered tigers and river dolphins, as well as nearly 300 species of birds.
Many residents also continue to suffer the after-effects of Cyclone Aila, which affected an estimated 100,000 people when it struck the Sundarbans in 2009, destroying local infrastructure and significantly changing the landscape in parts of the region.
The Sundarbans is also facing sea-level rise of roughly 3 centimetres a year, around twice the global average, according to the report. The rising sea level is displacing communities and damaging once-fertile soil.

Two accused confess in Rangpur's 4 murders case
item.description:
Two people arrested in connection with the killing of four family members, including a former schoolteacher, at their home in Rangpur city confessed to the murders before a court.
The accused, Mugdha Das, 23, and Siddhartha Das, 19, made their confessional statements before Rangpur Metropolitan Magistrate Rafiq-ul Islam at around 11:30pm on Sunday, said Nirmal Chandra, officer-in-charge (investigation) and investigating officer of the case.
He said both accused admitted their involvement in the incident and gave confessional statements before the court. However, he declined to disclose details of their statements, saying the matter was still under investigation.
The investigating officer also declined to comment on how or why the four members of the same family were killed.
After recording their confessional statements, the court ordered the two accused to be sent to Rangpur Central Jail, Nirmal Chandra said.
He said there was no provision to keep the accused in police custody after they had given confessional statements.
The two accused were taken to jail around 12:30am.

item.title: Tahura hat-trick helps Rajshahi Stars sign off AFC Women’s Champions League with 8-0 rout
item.description:
Tahura Khatun scored a hat-trick as Rajshahi Stars FC ended their AFC Women’s Champions League 2026/27 Preliminary Stage campaign in style with an emphatic 8-0 victory over Rovers FC of Guam on Sunday.
The Group A match at Likas Stadium saw the Bangladeshi side dominate from start to finish, with Shamsunnahar Jr. also scoring twice as Rajshahi Stars secured a confidence-boosting win in their debut continental campaign.
Rajshahi had already been eliminated from contention for a place in the main tournament after losing their opening two group matches, but head coach Golam Robbani’s side responded strongly to finish their campaign on a positive note.
Shamsunnahar opened the scoring in the third minute with a long-range effort from around 30 yards. Her speculative shot slipped through the hands of Rovers goalkeeper Jae Almonte and found the back of the net.
Rajshahi doubled their advantage in the 17th minute when Tahura side-footed home from close range after Sultana surged down the left and delivered a dangerous cross.
Tahura struck again eight minutes later, finishing from close range after Shamsunnahar sent a low ball across the face of goal to give Rajshahi a commanding 3-0 lead at halftime.
The Bangladesh side continued their relentless pressure after the break and added two goals in quick succession.
Rovers defender Marlena Connelley inadvertently turned the ball into her own net in the 53rd minute before Monika Chakma made it 5-0 moments later.
Tahura completed her hat-trick in the 60th minute, further underlining her impact in the final match of the campaign.
Shamsunnahar then added her second in the 71st minute before Shamsunnahar Sr completed the rout deep into stoppage time, scoring in the fifth minute of added time.
The comprehensive victory gave Rajshahi Stars a memorable finish to their first AFC Women’s Champions League appearance, although their earlier defeats meant they could not progress to the main tournament stage.

3 held over murder of Gazipur auto-rickshaw driver
item.description:
The Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) has arrested three people in connection with the killing of a 60-year-old auto-rickshaw driver in Kapasia, Gazipur, allegedly to steal his battery-powered vehicle. The victim’s 75-year-old mother also died of cardiac arrest after learning about her son’s death.
The deceased, Ataur Rahman alias Ata Mia, was killed on Thursday near Mirzanagar Girls’ High School in Dakkhin Gaogaan under Sonmania union. He had left home around 4pm with his auto-rickshaw, worth about Tk1.4 lakh, to earn a living. The attackers allegedly strangled him with a rope and struck him with an iron rod and hammer before fleeing with the vehicle and his mobile phone.
According to Gazipur PBI Superintendent of Police Md Rakibul Akter, Ataur left home around 4pm on Thursday with his auto-rickshaw, worth around Tk1.4 lakh, to earn a living.
The arrested suspects are Rajib Khan, Nakibul Hasan Rakib, both from Kapasia, and Mohammad Kibria, owner of Al-Madina Enterprise at Hatirdia bus stand in Narsingdi’s Monohardi.
A case was filed with Kapasia Police Station on Friday. The PBI later took over the investigation and arrested Rajib and Rakib within 24 hours using digital forensic analysis and confidential information.
Following their information, investigators recovered the stolen auto-rickshaw from Al-Madina Enterprise and arrested Kibria for allegedly purchasing and keeping the stolen vehicle. The PBI also recovered Tk22,000 from its sale and the weapons and rope allegedly used in the killing. The suspects reportedly sold the vehicle for Tk42,000 and shared the money.
According to the PBI, Rajib and Rakib confessed under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, saying they planned the robbery because of debt and targeted Ataur because Rakib was distantly related to him.

At Jharna Restaurant, guests can enjoy an exclusive four-course anniversary dinner, specially curated for the occasion and priced at Tk 4,500 per person, all-inclusive.

At Pool Café, every order of Steak, Salmon or Mixed Grill will include a complimentary anniversary dessert and soft drink. Guests can also enjoy 15 per cent off the Gueridon Salad Menu and Dine & Dive throughout the anniversary celebration.

item.title: Education support project funded by Bata Shoe Foundation officially inaugurated
item.description:
An education support project on the Literacy Portfolio and the Gender Equality Portfolio, funded by the Bata Shoe Foundation and implemented by Room to Read Bangladesh, was inaugurated today, Monday at Ashraf Textile Mills High School in Gazipur, reports a press release.

Under the project, and in line with PEDP4, activities have been built in for grades one through five of primary school, including the establishment of child-friendly classroom libraries, the supply of leveled storybooks, teacher training, and the selection of “Book Captains” to support building students’ regular reading habits.

Initiatives will also be taken to raise school attendance and foster a reading culture at home, including reading-play festivals, wall magazines, and parent meetings.

At the secondary level, alongside the formation of “Life-Skills Clubs” aimed at enabling students to make right decisions and progress into higher education, educational and learning materials have been distributed for club rooms, and teacher's guides and student workbooks have been supplied.

Training is also being arranged for teachers on Child Protection Policy (CPP), Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), and Sexual Harassment Prevention Committee (SHPC), and there are plans to hold Family Fairs to strengthen family and community engagement.

As chief guest at the inauguration ceremony, Professor Zahida Nazneen, director (Planning and Development Wing) of the Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education, inaugurated the Life-Skills Club Room, distributed materials, and formally launched the project activities.

Special guests included Razia Sultana, HR manager and Bata Children's Program Lead (APAC); Md Mizanur Rahman, assistant director (Planning and Development Wing) of the Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education; and Rakhi Sarkar, country director of Room to Read Bangladesh.

The event was chaired by Md Al Mamun Talukder, district education officer, Gazipur. A presentation on reading-habit development activities for children in primary schools was facilitated by Md Mazharul Karim, literacy director of Room to Read Bangladesh, and a presentation on life-skills development activities in secondary schools was facilitated by Iffat Zerin, Gender Equality Portfolio manager at Room to Read Bangladesh.

Speaking as a special guest, Razia Sultana, HR manager and Bata Children's Program Lead (APAC) said, “We are delighted to join this joint project with Room to Read. We are hopeful that it will help build a reading habit among children and help them grow into independent readers. At the same time, secondary students will gain the Life-Skills they need to continue their education.”

Speaking as a special guest, Rakhi Sarkar, country director of Room to Read Bangladesh, said, “Education is not just about passing exams or earning certificates; it is a process of learning to think, make sound decisions, and become a responsible citizen of society. Supported by the Bata Shoe Foundation, our Literacy and Gender Equality Portfolio is working to spread the joy of reading among children while building lifelong skills, leadership, and a safe learning environment in this school. I sincerely thank the Government of Bangladesh, school authorities, and teachers for their cooperation in this initiative.”

Professor Zahida Nazneen, chief guest of the event and Director (Planning and Development Wing) of the Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education, said, “Today's children are our future. By building a habit of reading at the primary level and gaining Life-Skills at the secondary level, students will be able to make sound decisions about their own lives and grow into good citizens. Room to Read's books are playing a unique role in building children's reading habits. In this process, the role of “Book Captains” — who support classmates who are falling behind — and of aware parents, is extremely important.”

Md Al Mamun Talukder, chair of the event and District Education Officer, Gazipur, said in his remarks, “If we can create a joyful reading environment for students in schools, they will be encouraged to come to school on their own. For this, school authorities need to be more proactive, and the knowledge gained from Room to Read's training must be applied regularly in the classroom. I wish this education support project every success.”

Room to Read, an international development organisation, has been providing education support since 2009 with approval from the Directorate of Primary Education — aimed at achieving quality education at the primary level — and the Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education — aimed at establishing educational equity at the secondary and higher-secondary levels.

It currently runs, with its own funding, activities to improve reading proficiency and build reading habits at the primary level in Natore, Narail, Dhaka, Moulvibazar, Jhalokati, Cox's Bazar, and Jamalpur, and, with USDA/WFP funding, in Habiganj.

Project-based activities are also being carried out with the Department of Public Libraries (DPL) in Narsingdi, Moulvibazar, and Cox's Bazar, and with the National Academy for Primary Education (NAPE) in Mymensingh.

To develop numeracy skills at the primary level, the development of supportive teaching-learning materials and teachers’ professional skills development activities also began in 2026.

Life-skills activities at the secondary school level, funded by Room to Read's own resources, are also ongoing in the first six districts named above.

item.title: Honourable Speaker, the ball is in your court
item.description:
Following the recent circulation of a video on social media, Jamaat-e-Islami expelled its Member of Parliament Gazi Nazrul Islam from the party and referred the matter to your office for appropriate action. To the best of our knowledge, no decision has yet been made in this regard.

In such a situation, there are precedents from the past. Former Speaker Jamiruddin Sircar did not cancel the membership of former BNP lawmaker Abu Hena. Later, when former Awami League minister Latif Siddiqui was expelled from the party, Speaker Shirin Sharmin Chaudhury referred the question of his parliamentary membership to the Election Commission for a decision. However, Mr. Siddiqui resigned before the Commission could reach a decision.
Thus, uncertainty still remains over whether those expelled from their political parties should retain their membership in Parliament. We believe, however, that the authority to make a decision regarding Mr. Islam rests with you, in your capacity as Speaker, as well as with the Parliament and the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Privileges constituted under your leadership.

Many may not know that our existing Constitution explicitly mentions two standing committees: one is the Public Accounts Committee, and the other is the Parliamentary Committee on Privileges. In other words, these two committees are of the highest importance, and they are also composed of some of the most important officeholders.

For example, in our 13th National Parliament, the Parliamentary Committee on Privileges has been formed with 10 members under the leadership of the Speaker. Its members include Prime Minister and Leader of the House Tarique Rahman, Leader of the Opposition Shafiqul Rahman, Deputy Speaker Kaiser Kamal, Mirza Abbas Uddin Ahmed, Gayeshwar Chandra Roy, Md. Nurul Islam, Zainul Abedin Farroque, and Nahid Islam.

Article 78 of the Constitution of Bangladesh concerns parliamentary privileges and immunities. Under its provisions, Parliament may regulate its own proceedings, and the courts have no jurisdiction to question such proceedings. The freedom of speech of members of Parliament is absolute, and this too falls outside the jurisdiction of the courts. To provide protection in these matters, Article 78(5) directs that a law concerning the privileges of Parliament and its members be enacted; however, such a law has not yet been enacted. It should be noted that Articles 76(2)(c) and (d), and 76(3) of the Constitution also relate to parliamentary privileges.

The concept of parliamentary privilege originated in the British Parliament. Writing on parliamentary matters in his famous treatise A Treatise on the Law, Privileges, Proceedings and Usage of Parliament, parliamentary scholar Erskine May wrote: “Parliamentary privilege is the sum of certain peculiar rights enjoyed by each House collectively and by members individually, without which they could not discharge their functions. These rights are additional to those possessed by other bodies or individuals, and therefore, although parliamentary privilege is part of the law of the land, it provides a degree of exemption from the ordinary law.”

What will happen to expelled Jamaat leader Gazi Nazrul's parliamentary seat?

Parliamentary privileges can be divided into two categories: those that apply individually to members of Parliament and those that apply to Parliament as a whole. More specifically, the privileges and immunities applicable to individual members of Parliament include: (a) freedom of speech; (b) exemption from arrest in civil cases; (c) exemption from serving on a jury (although this does not apply in our country); and (d) exemption from being required to appear as a witness. These are essentially rights relating to immunity, and they ensure that individual members of Parliament can perform their functions freely. Rules 172–176 of the Rules of Procedure of the Bangladesh National Parliament contain provisions relating to these matters.

The rights and powers applicable to Parliament as a whole include: (a) the right to maintain discipline. This includes the power to punish any person, including members of Parliament, for violating parliamentary privilege or committing contempt of Parliament, as well as the power to expel members of Parliament for corruption, misconduct, wrongdoing, or other improper conduct. Such powers of Parliament are known as disciplinary powers. (b) The power to manage Parliament’s internal affairs and regulate its procedures. (c) The power to ensure the attendance and effective functioning of Parliament. (d) The power to conduct inquiries and summon witnesses and documents. Rules 201–203 of the Rules of Procedure of our National Parliament contain provisions relating to these matters. (e) The power to administer oaths to witnesses. Rules 204–205 of our Rules of Procedure are relevant in this regard. (f) The power to publish documents containing defamatory material.

For a clearer understanding, it is necessary to distinguish between privilege, power, and immunity. According to Justice Subba Rao of the Supreme Court of India, the power of Parliament to exercise exclusive control over its own internal proceedings may be regarded as a privilege. The right to punish a person for violating or showing contempt of the privileges of Parliament may be described as a power. Immunity is the right of a member of Parliament not to be held liable for anything said by him in Parliament. [Special Reference, Article 143, AIR (1965) SC 745]

In our country, parliamentary privilege is generally regarded as something related to the rights and benefits enjoyed by members of Parliament, and therefore it is hardly ever considered applicable. Nevertheless, it was invoked in the case of some members of the Constituent Assembly after independence, particularly those who had collaborated with the Pakistanis. At that time, several members were also accused of abuse of power, corruption, and nepotism.

To the best of our knowledge, on 23 March 1972, a presidential order was issued providing for the cancellation of the membership of Constituent Assembly members with a view to taking action against those accused. Pursuant to that order, 16 members were expelled on 16 April 1972, on allegations of corruption. Subsequently, on 22 September the membership of another 19 members of the Constituent Assembly was cancelled.

By contrast, in neighbouring India, disciplinary action has been taken against many members of Parliament on allegations of misconduct. For example, in 2005, 11 members were expelled simultaneously from India’s Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha over allegations that they had accepted money in exchange for raising questions in Parliament and had engaged in irregularities in the use of funds allocated to members of Parliament for local development. The expulsions were subsequently challenged in court.

In Raja Ram Pal v. Speaker [(2007) 3 SCC], a Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court of India upheld the expulsions by a vote of 4–1. It is worth noting that the constitutional provisions relating to parliamentary privilege in India and Bangladesh are broadly similar.

Finally, the great Jatiya Sangsad, or “House of the People,” is the centre of parliamentary democracy, and the effectiveness of Parliament depends to a great extent on the competence, dedication, and character of its members. Through his conduct, Member of Parliament Gazi Nazrul Islam has undoubtedly brought the dignity and reputation of Parliament into disrepute in the eyes of the public. We therefore hope that the Honourable Speaker will, through the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Privileges constituted under his leadership, immediately initiate appropriate action against him and, if necessary, take steps to permanently expel him from Parliament.

Such action would also send an important message to other members of Parliament. At the same time, we hope that steps will be taken to enact a law on this matter promptly, in accordance with the constitutional directive. In this connection, it is pertinent to note that in the referendum held on February 12 (Item No. 48), the people gave their consent to the enactment of this law.

* Dr. Badiul Alam Majumdar, Secretary, Shujan (Citizens for Good Governance)
* The views expressed here are those of the author.
* This article appeared in Prothom Alo print and online and has been translated by Ayesha Kabir for Prothom Alo English Online

item.title: Forest rangers attacked when reclaiming hills and forests in Rangunia
item.description:
Across the Karnaphuli River from Chandraghona Lichubagan in Rangunia, Chattogram, lies the Kodala Forest Beat. The scars of hill cutting, new settlements and tree stumps are visible across the landscape.

A few days spent visiting several areas of Rangunia in July revealed a similar picture in the Kodala, Narischha, Chiringa, Pomra and Nishchintapur forest beats. In some places, roads had been cut into hills to transport soil; elsewhere, new houses had been built, while the remains of felled trees pointed to ongoing logging.

Local residents and forest officials said that before 5 August 2024, businesses involving forests, hills and sand were controlled by followers of former minister Hasan Mahmud.

During the Awami League government, more than 212 acres of Forest Department land in Rangunia were illegally occupied, much of it allegedly by Hasan Mahmud’s brother Ershad Mahmud. Around 200 acres under his control were recovered in August 2024 after the government fell.

Yet illegal occupation and tree smuggling have continued. The Forest Department says about 2,000 acres of forestland in Rangunia remain occupied, a large portion of it allegedly taken over by people using the names and political identities of local BNP and Jubo Dal leaders and activists.

Signs of forest and hill destruction

Signs of deforestation and hill cutting can be seen across Rangunia. Agricultural land and hills have been cut in Islampur union along the Rangamati road. Extensive earth-cutting has also been observed in Mohammadpur and Golachipa areas of South Rajanagar union.

The roughly 3,300-acre Kodala Forest Beat is largely hilly forestland. Visits to Chandraghona Bongram, Segunbagan, Kolabaijyaghona, Bottoli, Dhuillyachhari, Nishchintapur, Foittyagoda and Mahutverghona revealed widespread forest encroachment, hill cutting and tree smuggling.

Residents said hill cutting resumes after short pauses. Soil is generally removed at night, loaded onto trucks and transported to ponds, canals, water bodies, paddy fields and various land-filling projects.

Some locals claimed that more than 100 trucks carry away soil on certain nights.

Forest officials said those involved in hill cutting and forest encroachment have armed supporters and political influence, making it difficult for the limited number of forest personnel to stop them. Rangers have also faced attacks during drives against illegal activities.

Forest officials attacked

Former Kodala Forest Beat deputy ranger KM Mahmudul Hasan was attacked during one such operation. Forest officials said he was repeatedly hacked with sharp weapons. Other forest workers have also been assaulted and threatened at various times.

According to a general diary filed with Rangunia police, between 12:30am and 5:00 am on 7 March, 2025, around 40 to 45 armed men locked Kodala beat officer Khondkar Mahabubur Rahman and his colleagues inside their office. They also took away their mobile phones. The GD said the men were carrying machetes, kiriches, knives, iron rods and other locally made weapons.

The men allegedly cut down and removed 24 teak trees from Segunbagan in South Jungle Nishchintapur of Chandraghona union while keeping the forest officials confined. The GD also said the attackers threatened to kill the officials if they informed police or senior authorities.

An official who took part in the operation said hundreds of people gather whenever forest personnel attempt to remove illegal structures from forestland and chase them away.

According to the Forest Department, forest officials have had to fire around 30 rounds during operations over the past 18 months to confront armed forest robbers and encroachers. The encroachers have also fired back. In the previous two years, only two rounds had been fired during operations in the Kodala beat.

Forest officials said that even firing warning shots has failed to completely stop hill cutting and encroachment. When one group is removed, another often returns after a few days and begins constructing houses under a different identity.

A similar situation was found in the Chiringa Forest Beat. Forest guard Khokon Das told Prothom Alo that frequent killings and clashes in the area put everyone, including forest personnel, at risk.

Encroachment and smuggling under political identities

Only four people, including a deputy ranger and forest personnel, are currently assigned to the Kodala Forest Beat. Officials said it is almost impossible for such a small team to prevent tree felling and smuggling, stop encroachment and simultaneously handle related legal cases.

After the political change on 5 August 2024, the Kodala Forest Beat office was attacked and looted. Seized timber, furniture and other materials were taken away, and the office was set on fire.

Local residents alleged that after the change in government, several BNP and Jubo Dal leaders and activists in the Chandraghona-Kadamtali area became involved in occupying forests and hills by using their political identities. Several names also appear on Forest Department lists: Chandraghona Ward 9 BNP president Ahmadul Haque, Lichubagan CNG Drivers’ Association president and BNP activist Abdul Mannan alias Monu, Jubo Dal activist Juel, his brother Md Sohel and Kefayet Ullah.

Ahmadul Haque denied the allegations, saying, “On the contrary, I have protected the resources in the forest beat.” Abdul Mannan and Juel also denied involvement when contacted by phone.

Local and Forest Department sources said a timber-carrying vehicle used by Juel was seized by the BGB and handed over to the Kaptai Forest Department. Sohel has been accused of supplying bricks and sand to houses built on occupied forestland.

Khondkar Mahabubur Rahman, deputy ranger of the Kodala Forest Beat, said that despite the shortage of manpower, they were making every effort to protect the forest. Cases were being filed regularly and smuggled timber was being seized. However, he said forest personnel constantly face various risks and threats.

GDs filed, but encroachment continues

Forest officials filed at least 10 general diaries with Rangunia police during the first six months of this year over threats and attempts to attack them. The GDs said people gathered to obstruct operations when officials tried to evict illegal settlers or prevent the occupation of forestland and felling of trees. In many cases, attempts were made to attack forest guards, allegedly under the leadership of local political figures.

Mohammad Sohel Rana, divisional forest officer of Chattogram South Forest Division, told Prothom Alo, “Encroachers sometimes try to attack us when we conduct recovery drives. Something similar happened recently after an operation in Dhopachhari. However, whenever we receive information, we go with the necessary preparations. We also seek assistance from the police and upazila administration.”

A local resident who witnessed several operations in the Kodala Forest Beat said the encroachers move around in large groups, many carrying weapons. A small number of forest officials cannot stand up to them, he said.

In his view, coordinated operations involving the police, army, BGB, district administration and Forest Department are needed to free the forests from encroachment. But first, he said, there must be a political decision that no one will be allowed to occupy forestland using the identity of any political party.

A Forest Department official warned that if deforestation and hill cutting continue at the current rate, there may be no forest left in the area within 10 years. More than 100 houses were reportedly attempted to be built in the Kodala beat alone this year.

There are leaders in almost every household now, the official said. Without political action, the Forest Department alone cannot protect these forests.

item.title: Feni’s Nusrat Jahan murder case: Death sentences of two convicts upheld
item.description:
The High Court has upheld the death sentences of two accused in the sensational murder case of madrasah student Nusrat Jahan Rafi in Sonagazi, Feni.

A High Court bench comprising Justice Bhishmadev Chakraborty and Justice KM Rasheduzzaman Raja delivered the verdict today, Monday, after hearing the death reference (approval of the death sentences), appeals and jail appeals filed in the case.

Arrest warrant issued against ex-Sonagazi OC over Nusrat murder

The two convicts whose death sentences have been upheld are Siraj Ud Doula, then principal of Sonagazi Islamia Fazil (Degree) Madrasah, and Shahadat Hossain Shamim.

The Feni Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunal delivered its verdict in the case on 24 October 2019. It sentenced 16 people, including the madrasa’s suspended principal Siraj Ud Doula, to death.

According to case documents, on 27 March 2019, then principal Siraj Ud Doula called Nusrat to his office at Sonagazi Islamia Fazil (Degree) Madrasa and sexually harassed her. He was arrested after a case was filed over the incident.

Nusrat murder: Charges against ex-Sonagazi OC found true

When Nusrat refused to withdraw the case, she was called to the madrasa’s rooftop on 6 April, where her hands and feet were tied, kerosene was poured over her and she was set on fire.

Nusrat died on 10 April that year while undergoing treatment at the burn unit of Dhaka Medical College Hospital. Her elder brother Mahmudul Hasan (Noman) filed a case with Sonagazi police station over the arson attack. The case was later converted into a murder case.

After the trial court verdict, the case records were sent to the relevant High Court section on 29 October 2019 for a death reference and registered as Death Reference No. 140/2019.

Former Sonagazi OC Moazzem jailed for 8 years

A paper book was prepared on a priority basis because the case was considered sensational. The convicts also filed separate appeals and jail appeals.

On 10 June, the chief justice constituted a specific High Court bench to hear death references, appeals and miscellaneous matters related to the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act on a priority basis. The bench began its proceedings on 14 June.

The hearing in this sensational murder case began before the bench on 28 July and concluded on 20 August. On that day, the High Court fixed 24 August for the verdict. Accordingly, the verdict was delivered today.

item.title: 4 killed in Rangpur: Funerals held side by side
item.description:
The funeral rites for retired Rangpur Zilla School teacher Ganapati Chakraborty, his wife and their two children were completed at around 10:30 pm yesterday, Sunday, at Kamal Kachhna Dakhiganj Mohashashan in Rangpur city.

Earlier, at around 7 pm yesterday, Sunday police handed over the bodies of the four victims to their family members after completing the post-mortem examinations at Rangpur Medical College Hospital.

The bodies were then taken to the Mohashashan by ambulance in two trips. In accordance with Hindu religious rituals, the family placed the four bodies on four pyres side by side. The cremation ceremony ended at around 10:30 pm.

'Who killed my sister, brother-in-law and their children?

Witnesses said the scene became heartbreaking when the four bodies were placed on the pyres. Relatives wept, while even acquaintances outside the family struggled to hold back their tears.

Biswajit Chakraborty, son-in-law of the deceased teacher’s elder brother, took part in the cremation.

He said, “I have witnessed many funerals in my life. The painful sight of bidding farewell to four people at the same time will remain in my memory until the last day of my life.”

Bodies of former Rangpur zilla school teacher, wife and 2 children recovered

Puja Chakraborty, sister-in-law of the deceased teacher, broke down in tears while performing the last rites of her sister, brother-in-law, niece and nephew.

She said, “God will judge those who killed them. I want them to receive severe punishment.” After pausing for a moment, she said, “They were supposed to be alive today. They all departed together!”

At around 3:30 am on Saturday, police recovered the bodies of Ganapati Chakraborty, his wife Pritilata Chakraborty, their daughter Agami Chakraborty, who had completed a Master’s degree in English, and their son Ayush Chakraborty, a fifth-grade student, from their home in Machuapara, in the Kamal Kachna area of Rangpur city.

Police alleged that the victims were strangled one after another after they protested against the use of yaba.

In connection with the incident, two young men, Siddhartha Das and Mugdha Das, were arrested and sent to jail. Both are residents of Machuapara.

item.title: Trivedi: India seeks stronger business ties with Bangladesh
item.description:
Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi on Monday laid emphasis on strengthening business-to-business relations between the two countries, saying politics will continue on its own course.
“Let us have business-to-business together. Politics will continue in its own way, but it is our responsibility to deliver what people deserve. I have no doubt that the future is very positive. Let things take their own time, and let us work together for the people of both countries,” he told reporters at Secretariat after a meeting with Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir.
The high commissioner said Bangladesh is a vibrant, sovereign and independent country, just as India is.
“Nobody is big and nobody is small. We are all equals, and we have to work on that footing,” the Indian envoy said.
Highlighting the importance of peace and prosperity, Trivedi said prosperity would follow if peace could be ensured.
“I think it is the responsibility of both countries to ensure peace and prosperity for the young generation,” he said.
The envoy said ordinary people do not ask for much; they want the basic necessities of life, with peace being their foremost priority.
Referring to Mahatma Gandhi, the high commissioner said that whatever decision is taken, leaders must always consider its impact on the poorest people.
Trivedi also stressed the need to explore joint-venture business opportunities in Bangladesh, including projects in border areas.
Highlighting the importance of economic and people-to-people ties, the High Commissioner recently, at a reception, said the private sector has a crucial role in bridging differences between the two countries.
"No government in the world can provide everything. It always needs the private sector," he said, expressing gratitude to the business communities on both sides.

item.title: 440 arrested in police operation in Dhaka
item.description:
A total of 440 people were arrested in a regular operation by the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) across the capital over the past 24 hours. During the operation, 46 cases were filed at different police stations.
Additional Deputy Commissioner of the DMP’s Media and Public Relations Division, Niaz Mehedi, disclosed the information on Monday.
According to the DMP, 29 people were arrested by the Ramna Division, 45 by the Lalbagh Division, 50 by the Wari Division, 36 by the Motijheel Division, 67 by the Tejgaon Division, 127 by the Mirpur Division, 31 by the Gulshan Division, 50 by the Uttara Division, and five by the Detective Branch (DB).
During the operation, police recovered one foreign-made pistol, one magazine, six rounds of ammunition, one sword, one knife, and one grenade. They also seized 12.5 kilograms of cannabis, 39,127 yaba tablets, 3.2 grams of powdered yaba, one motorcycle, nine mobile phones, and Tk 3,000 in cash. In addition, two victims were rescued.
The DMP official said the arrests were made during operations conducted in various police station areas across the capital, during which the aforementioned evidence and narcotics were recovered.
Legal proceedings against the arrested individuals are currently underway.

item.title: UEFA chief Ceferin rules out bid to replace Infantino as FIFA president
item.description:
UEFA chief Aleksander Ceferin has said he is "not interested" in replacing Gianni Infantino, but has warned the under-fire FIFA president must either quit or face a leadership challenge in March.
Infantino has come under increasing pressure to step down as the head of world football's global governing body over his now abandoned plan to secure private investment in FIFA tournaments, including the men's and women's World Cups.
Meanwhile UEFA, which oversees the running of European football, has threatened a boycott of FIFA competitions, with several continental and national federations also withdrawing their support for Infantino.
But Ceferin ruled himself out of a bid to take Infantino's place as the chief of world football, the 58-year-old Slovenian on Monday telling The Rest is Politics podcast: "I'm not interested because of two reasons. One reason is that I love UEFA and I love working here, and I think that at a certain point... it's time to also enjoy life a bit.
"And the second point is, my credibility is much, much higher if I'm not interested in the position."
Ceferin has been vocal in his criticism since Infantino revealed his controversial plans to seek private investment in a company to run FIFA tournaments.
He now believes Infantino's previously impregnable position is under threat, with Ceferin forecasting he will have to stand down or face a leadership challenge if he seeks re-election at the next FIFA Congress in Morocco in March 2027.
Infantino, a former UEFA secretary general, had the broad backing of European nations when he succeeded Sepp Blatter as FIFA president in 2016.
But Ceferin, who revealed he has not spoken to Infantino since the start of the controversy, insisted the current situation was very different.
"There are two options," he said. "One option is that he (Infantino) realises that he doesn't have the support, and that's not only a political support of the ones who vote, but the political support of football community, the political support of fans, the political support of the players, former players, coaches.
"And the second option that he goes to the elections in March, but in that case, I think he will have a candidate against him. I don't know yet who."
CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani and AFC boss Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim al-Khalifa are considered two of the most likely challengers for Infantino's position.

item.title: Kane voted player of the year in Germany
item.description:
Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane was voted the 2026 player of the year in Germany by an association of sports journalists on Sunday, finishing ahead of teammate Michael Olise.
The England captain won the award after a stellar season, winning the Bundesliga and German Cup while Bayern also reached the Champions League semi-finals.Kane scored 61 goals for the club last season in all competitions.
He then scored six goals as England reached the World Cup semi-finals before losing to Argentina.
Bayern boss Vincent Kompany was named coach of the year, while their women's captain Giulia Gwinn won the award for best female player.
The 695 members of the German sports journalists association vote on the award, with Bundesliga players or German footballers playing abroad eligible for the honour.
Kane, 33, is the first Englishman to win the award while Olise also finished second in 2025, behind Florian Wirtz.
"It's almost impossible to find the right superlatives to describe Harry Kane -- sometimes I'm at a loss for words," Bayern sporting director Max Eberl said in a statement.
"He's already been named England's Footballer of the Year, and now he's also won it in Germany."
The England captain is among the favourites for the Ballon d'Or, which will be handed out in London in October.

item.title: Gauff powers past Pegula to win US Open warm-up in Cincinnati
item.description:
Coco Gauff made a statement Sunday with the US Open approaching, dominating Jessica Pegula 6-2, 6-4 to win her first title of 2026 at the WTA 1000 in Cincinnati.
World number four Gauff claimed her first WTA title since last October in Wuhan, having come up short in finals in Miami and Rome this year.
Her victory over third-ranked Pegula gave her a second Cincinnati crown. Gauff earned her first in 2023, going on to claim the first of her two Grand Slam titles at the US Open that year.
The first all-American WTA final in Cincinnati since Rosie Casals beat Nancy Richey in 1970 was a lopsided affair.
Gauff insisted it shouldn't be considered a barometer for the US Open, but admitted it was a welcome confidence boost.
"I don't think that this is an indicator that I'm going to do well in New York or anything like that to be honest," Gauff said, but added: "(I'm going in) knowing that I can figure out these matches (even if) I'm not playing my best, but also knowing that I can play that great tennis that I felt I was playing this week.
"Hopefully I can use the experience here in New York."
Gauff polished off an impressive tournament with victory in 75 minutes and will head to New York riding a wave of confidence for the start of the US Open next Sunday.
It's a far cry from an early exit in Cincinnati last year, which Gauff said left her "in the parking lot in tears" after she coughed up 16 double-faults in defeat.
"It's a big difference, what a year can make," added Gauff, who was so bothered by her service struggles this time last year that she hired a new coach days before the US Open.
"Last year I was just frustrated with my game, and I felt like I was declining," she said. "It's not something any player wants to feel. You always want to feel like you're getting better, at the worst, like just plateauing."
- 'Amazing momentum' -
This time around Gauff was rock-solid on serve and Pegula, coming off a hard-fought win over defending champion Iga Swiatek, had no answer for Gauff's speed and aggression.
Gauff broke Pegula twice for a 4-0 lead and was up 5-0 before Pegula got on the scoreboard, holding serve and clawing back a break.
It was a brief reprieve as Gauff broke again to pocket the opening set after 34 minutes.
The second set was more of the same, Gauff breaking on the way to a 3-0 lead and Pegula playing catch-up.
Gauff sealed victory on her first match point to conclude 12 days of tennis at the sprawling Midwest venue.
Gauff's win squared the career series between the two at five wins each. Gauff won her second match this season against Pegula after defeating her compatriot in a Wimbledon quarter-final.
Pegula was not displeased with her own performance heading into the final Grand Slam of the season.
"I don't think I played bad but you played a very high level, it was not fun to play against," she told Gauff during the trophy ceremony.
"You have amazing momentum heading into the US Open."

item.title: Amorim starts Serie A life with Milan win, Juve edge Frosinone
item.description:
Former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim made a winning start to life in Serie A as his AC Milan side opened their campaign with a 2-1 victory at Torino on Sunday, after Juventus got underway with an unconvincing win.
The Rossoneri turned to Amorim after finishing fifth last season, and the Portuguese has been provided with an overhauled squad as the giants look to challenge their city rivals and defending champions, Inter Milan.
Amorim had to wait until the hour mark for his side to capitalise on their dominance in Piedmont.
The breakthrough came shortly after the hour thanks to teenage debutant Alphadjo Cisse's deft opener, which completely removed the shackles from Milan.
Adrien Rabiot doubled the lead minutes later when he ghosted onto Samuel Chukwueze's back-post cross.
Marquee summer signing Goncalo Ramos, who joined from Paris Saint-Germain for 74 million euros ($86 million), failed to find the net but caused the Torino defence no end of trouble.
The gloss was somewhat taken off the result in the dying moments of stoppage time as Milan goalkeeper Mike Maignan was beaten by a looping volley from Che Adams.
"The most important thing is to win," Amorim told DAZN.
"We talk about ways of playing, but there is one goal in football, winning."
Atalanta, also with a new man at the helm in the shape of former Chelsea and Napoli boss Maurizio Sarri, kicked off their season with a 2-1 win at home to Sassuolo.
The 2024 Europa League winners took an early lead courtesy of a Giacomo Raspadori piledriver, before Cas Odenthal hit back from close range for the visitors on 55 minutes.
But Nikola Krstovic took advantage of sloppy defending 10 minutes later to ensure Atalanta would earn all three points.
- 'A bit light' -
Earlier, Juventus secured a 1-0 away win against newly promoted Frosinone, but failed to impress in their campaign-opener.
Juve, who finished a disappointing sixth last season, secured all three points thanks to Gleison Bremer's 22nd-minute header.
Luciano Spalletti's side then dominated proceedings but failed to put the game beyond doubt.
Goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario, on loan from Tottenham Hotspur, had an issue with cramp and had to be substituted late on as a precaution, according to Spalletti, which nearly cost Juve dearly, as Frosinone pressed hard in stoppage time and hit the crossbar.
The Bianconeri, however, secured the result they needed, following in the footsteps of reigning champions Inter Milan, who thrashed another newly-promoted side, Monza, 4-1 on Saturday in the season opener.
"I would have preferred the team to show it has an identity, and it did that," Spalletti said. "At certain moments we're a bit light, we're not good at bringing that determination. But it can happen, especially at the start. We'll work on it."
Lecce made a strong start to the season against the third promoted side, Venezia, on Sunday as they defeated their hosts 2-0 courtesy of second-half goals from Olaf Gorter and Tiago Gabriel.
